tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

block.text:
Let me understand the task: create a single-page Three.js sci-fi hangar including the following:
- Hovering drones
- Blinking warning lights
- Emissive runway strips
- Understated volumetric-style fog planes
- Drone formation toggle
- Cinematic camera path
- Output a single self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript

"Self-contained" — Three.js itself needs to be either inlined or loaded from a CDN. Self-contained with inline JavaScript — I think it means a single HTML file (no separate JS/CSS files). Inlining the entire Three.js library would be huge. The common approach: use a CDN import (importmap) for three.module.js and inline all the custom JS. That's what most people mean by "single HTML file". Alternatively, I could write my own minimal WebGL... no, let's use a CDN import for three and inline all the custom code. That's the practical interpretation: one file, inline JS.

I could also consider writing it without a CDN using my own mini 3D math, but that would be a massive amount of work and low quality. Let's use a CDN import for three (with ES module importmap) and inline everything else. Note this in the file header.

Let me design the scene:

**Scene layout:**
- Hangar: large rectangular interior — floor with grid texture (procedural canvas texture), walls, ceiling with trusses (boxes), big hangar doors at one end.
- Runway strips: emissive strips on the floor leading to the hangar door, maybe a landing pad circle for the drones. Blinking (pulsing) emissive material.
- Drones: small drone geometry built from boxes/cylinders — body, 4 arms, rotor discs (rotating), hover animation with sine-wave bobbing, slight up-down motion, LED lights (emissive small spheres).
- Warning lights: rotating beacons — red rotating lights on wall posts or the ceiling, using emissive material + point lights (keep point light count low). Also a blinking hazard lamp bar (strip) near the hangar door.
- Fog planes: understated volumetric-style — a stack of large transparent planes with a procedurally drawn soft-gradient canvas texture (radial blob), low opacity, slowly moving, additive blending, near the floor. Also use scene.fog for depth.
- Formation toggle: UI button (or key F) to toggle between "formation" (grid/line) and "scatter" (orbit/random hover). Drones lerp smoothly between formation and scatter positions. Maybe two formations: grid vs circle. The requirement is "drone formation toggle" — so a toggle between form/loose. Toggle between 2 formations: "grid" and "circle" (or "scatter"). Button toggles; drones tween.
- Cinematic camera path: a CatmullRomCurve3 path circling the hangar, camera moves along it and looks at drones/center. Button/checkbox to enable cinematic mode, or key C. When off, OrbitControls? OrbitControls requires importing the addon; I could implement a simple manual orbit (drag to orbit) myself to keep the file self-contained (single import from CDN for three core only). Actually, addon import via CDN is also fine, but a simple manual orbit is easy and robust: mouse drag to orbit + wheel to zoom, with damping. Let me implement a minimal custom orbit control to avoid a second CDN file. Cinematic path: camera follows a Catmull-Rom closed curve, with a lookAt target (interpolated to drones or center), and the user can disable it with a button/key.

**Lighting:**
- Dim ambient/hemisphere light.
- A few point lights: warm key light, cyan rim. Keep count low (about 3–5 point lights) for performance.
- Emissive materials do most of the work (runway strips, drone LEDs, beacon lights).
- Fog: THREE.FogExp2 in a dark bluish color for depth.
- Optionally bloom via post-processing — adds imports (EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass). The bloom addon can also be imported from CDN. That would greatly improve the sci-fi look. But more CDN dependencies. content.text:
Let me understand the task: create a single-page Three.js sci-fi hangar including the following:
- Hovering drones
- Blinking warning lights
- Emissive runway strips
- Understated volumetric-style fog planes
- Drone formation toggle
- Cinematic camera path
- Output a single self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript

"Self-contained" — Three.js itself needs to be either inlined or loaded from a CDN. Self-contained with inline JavaScript — I think it means a single HTML file (no separate JS/CSS files). Inlining the entire Three.js library would be huge. The common approach: use a CDN import (importmap) for three.module.js and inline all the custom JS. summary.text:
## Primary Request and Intent
- Verbatim: "Build a single-page Three.js sci-fi hangar with hovering drones, animated warning lights, emissive runway strips, and subtle volumetric-style fog planes. Include drone formation toggle and cinematic camera path. Output one self-contained HTML file with inline JavaScript."
- Deliverable: one HTML file (all app JS/CSS inline) in workspace `/Users/alvin/claude-cowork/hangar20-dsh/`.
- Session constraints: approval prompts disabled (no `sandbox_permissions` escalation ever), DSH file policy danger-full-access, current dir `/Users/alvin/claude-cowork/hangar20-dsh` (was empty at start).

## Key Technical Concepts
- Three.js r160.0 pinned, loaded via dynamic `import()` from 3 CDN fallbacks (jsdelivr → unpkg → cdnjs); only external dependency (all else procedural/inline). All 3 URLs verified HTTP 200.
- Physical lighting (r160 default `useLegacyLights=false`): PointLight intensities in candela (320/240/90, beacon 6–60), decay 2; HemisphereLight 0.5.
- `ACESFilmicToneMapping`, exposure 1.12, `SRGBColorSpace`, `FogExp2(0x070b13, 0.011)`; additive-blended sprites/planes with `fog:false` for glow, `depthWrite:false`.
- All textures procedural via `CanvasTexture` (radial glow, fog blobs, door-light shaft, beam fade, 1024×2048 floor grid/scuffs/lanes, starfield+planet sky, hazard stripes, glowing wall sign).
- Room is single-sided planes → exterior viewpoints get a cutaway dollhouse view (backface culling) — deliberate property.
- Drone animation: lerp toward mode-specific target (`1 - Math.exp(-2.2*dt)`), shortest-arc yaw, bank from lateral velocity, rotor spin, LED blink, per-drone soft shadow disc.
- Camera: custom damped orbit (drag/scroll; phi clamp 0.15–1.45, r clamp 6–55) + closed centripetal `CatmullRomCurve3` cinematic path (8 pts, 85 s, lookAt lerps pad center ↔ drone 0); both modes produce a desired pose, actual camera/lookAt exp-lerped → smooth handoff.
- Headless smoke-test technique: Node + Proxy-stubbed WebGL/2D-canvas/document/window; three's `WebGLAnimation` uses `self.requestAnimationFrame` (line 29514 of three.mjs) so a captured rAF callback drives frames manually.

## Files and Code
- `/Users/alvin/claude-cowork/hangar20-dsh/hangar20.html` — THE DELIVERABLE (~800 lines). Structure: `<style>` (HUD/buttons/vignette/scanlines), `<body>` HUD (`#hud`, `#status` with `#s-form`/`#s-cam`/`#s-uav`, buttons `#b-form`/`#b-cam`/`#b-reset`, `#hint`, `#err`), one `<script type="module">`:
  - `loadThree()` (3 CDN urls), `fatal(html)`, top-level `try { THREE = await loadThree(); start(THREE); } catch { fatal(...) }`.
  - `start(THREE)`: renderer (antialias, pixelRatio≤2); textures `glowTex/fogTex/shaftTex/beamTex/floorTex/skyTex/hazardTex/signTex`; materials (`matFloor/matWall/matWall2/matCeil/matTruss/matDark/matDrone/matDroneDark/matSlat`).
  - Room: W=56 H=16 D=120 (HW=28 HD=60); opening openW=36 openH=13 at z=+60; 5 slats at top of opening (light spills below y≈6.8); sky plane 220×90 at z=68; doorGlow + floor pool (0,0.05,49); trusses at z=-45/-15/15/45; ribs every 8m; 4 windows; sign at (-27.92,9,34); service door at (10,3,-59.85); 4 ceiling strips (flicker).
  - Runway: `addStripSeg(x,z,w,l,color)` → `runSegs` (side strips x=±7 z 56→-14 step 2.6, 0x2fd4ff; center dashes step 4.5, 0xffb347; `d = 56 - z`); pad at (0,-20): 28-seg ring r=8.5 (chase), RingGeometry decal 7.9–9.1, cross decals; hazard decal (0,0.02,58).
  - Warnings: `makeBeacon(x,z,color,sweep)` ×3 → beacons[] (red (±15,44), amber (-14,-50)); 10-seg marching `barSegs` at y 13.55 z 59.38; 4 `strobes[]`.
  - Lights: hemi + padLight (0,13.5,-20) 320cd + doorLight (0,7,52) 240cd + backLight (0,10,-45) 90cd.
  - Fog: 11 `fogPlanes[]` (groups, additive, opacity 0.028–0.06, slow rot); 3 `mist[]` shaft planes z 54/56.5/58.5; `dust` Points (260) at (0,0,39).
  - Drones: 8 × `makeDrone(i)` (body 1.1×0.34×1.6, dome, fins, 4 arms/rotors (disc 0.55 + 1 blade 1.05), ledF cyan/ledB amber, thruster sprite, shadow disc); `slot` grid (x=(i%4−1.5)×4.5, y=4+0.7·row, z=−20∓2.5), `anchor` golden-angle (i×2.39996, r=3.5+(i%4)×2.4, y=2.6+(i%3)×1.4), `orbitR`/`orbitS`.
  - Camera/UI/anim: `orbit` init `{theta:0.55, phi:1.18, r:30}` target (0,3,-20); `camPos=(16,7,44)`; `camPts[8]`; `CAM_DUR=85`; `padLook=(0,3.2,-20)`; `ringBase=new THREE.Color(0.3,0.85,1)`; `animate()` updates all systems; `renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate)`.
- `/tmp/hangar20_check.mjs` — module JS extracted via `awk '/<script type="module">/{f=1;next} /<\/script>/{if(f){f=0}} f' hangar20.html`; passes `node --check` (745 lines).
- `/tmp/three.mjs` — downloaded three@0.160.0 module (416 exported names; all 31 `THREE.*` names used in the app resolve).
- `/tmp/h20_test/hangar_app.mjs` — copy of extracted module with all 3 CDN URLs sed-replaced to `file:///tmp/three.mjs`.
- `/tmp/h20_test/harness.mjs` — Node smoke test: stubs `window/self/globalThis`, `Object.defineProperty(globalThis,'navigator',{value:{userAgent:'node-smoke'},configurable:true})`, `document` (createElement/createElementNS→canvas stub, getElementById→el stub, body), rAF capture (`handlers.raf`), Proxy `makeGL()` (paramTable, makers list, getParameter/getError/isContextLost/getExtension/getShaderParameter→true/getShaderPrecisionFormat→{precision:23,rangeMin:127,rangeMax:127}/checkFramebufferStatus→0x8cd5, default no-op fns) and Proxy `make2d()`. Flow: `await import('./hangar_app.mjs')` → 5 frames → keydown f/c/r + resize → 3 more frames → "SMOKE TEST PASSED".

## Errors and Fixes
- Initial `write` of hangar20.html never landed (workspace empty on resume) → rewrote the entire file in one pass.
- Leftover debug code in drone update (`a0(d)` hack; malformed `const vz = (d.g.position.x && 0)`) → replaced with clean `oa` orbit-angle variable, analytic velocity heading, scalar right-vector banking.
- `ringBase` declared per-frame inside `animate()` + then orphaned by a bad edit → single `const ringBase = new THREE.Color(0.3,0.85,1)` in shared temporaries; duplicate in-loop decl removed.
- Stray `function a0(d) { return 0; }` → deleted.
- Initial camera outside volume (r=34, φ=1.12 → y≈17.6 > ceiling 16; camPos x=28 on wall) → orbit init φ=1.18 r=30 (y≈14.4), `camPos=(16,7,44)`, `resetCam()` matched.
- Edit-tool "file changed since it was read" → re-read the region, retried successfully.
- Harness run 1: `TypeError: Cannot set property navigator of #<Object> which has only a getter` (Node 24) → `Object.defineProperty`.
- Harness run 2: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'precision')` at `getMaxPrecision` (three.mjs:15805) → stubbed `getShaderPrecisionFormat`.
- Harness run 3 (CURRENT, unfixed): `TypeError: glVersion.indexOf is not a function` at `new WebGLState` (three.mjs:23015) — `getParameter(gl.VERSION)` returned a number because paramTable keys are strings (`'VERSION'` etc.) while lookup key is the numeric GL constant (VERSION=0x1F02=7938, VENDOR=7936, RENDERER=7937); `paramTable[7938]` → undefined → fell through to `?? 1024`.

## Pending Jobs
- Finish headless smoke test: fix harness `getParameter` stub to return strings for the numeric GL constants (7936/7937/7938 → e.g. `'WebGL 1.0 (stub)'`), re-run `cd /tmp/h20_test && node harness.mjs`, iterate on any further stub gaps until "SMOKE TEST PASSED".
- Then final user-facing summary of the deliverable (file path, features, how to run: open directly in a browser — three.js needs network, or serve locally; note single external CDN dep).

## Current Work
- Iterating on the headless smoke test for the completed `/Users/alvin/claude-cowork/hangar20-dsh/hangar20.html`. Last command: `cd /tmp/h20_test && node harness.mjs` → failed with `TypeError: glVersion.indexOf is not a function at new WebGLState (three.mjs:23015)`. Root cause identified: harness `getParameter` stub returns `paramTable[name] ?? 1024`, but `name` is the numeric GL constant (7936/7937/7938) while `paramTable` uses string keys (`VERSION`, `VENDOR`, `RENDERER`), so `gl.VERSION` yields `1024` (number) instead of a string, breaking `glVersion.indexOf('WebGL 2.1')` inside `new WebGLState`.
- Everything else verified: JS syntax (`node --check` OK), all 31 used THREE API names resolve against r160 exports, all 3 CDN URLs return 200, app imports and constructs scene graph successfully under stubs up to renderer init.

## Next Step
- Edit `/tmp/h20_test/harness.mjs` `getParameter` stub to special-case the string-returning constants, e.g.:
  ```js
  if (p === 'getParameter') return (name) => {
    if (name === 7936 || name === 7937 || name === 7938) return 'WebGL 1.0 (stub)'; // VENDOR / RENDERER / VERSION
    return paramTable[name] ?? 1024;
  };
  ```
  then re-run `cd /tmp/h20_test && node harness.mjs`; if more stub gaps surface (other constants needing string/array return values), patch similarly until "SMOKE TEST PASSED: scene built, 8 frames rendered" prints, then deliver the final summary of `hangar20.html` to the user.

## Critical Context
- Design intent: moody dark-blue hangar, emissive-driven look (no post-processing/bloom — glow faked with additive sprites/planes); ~350–400 draw calls total, fine for desktop.
- three.js pinned to 0.160.0 deliberately (stable API, no addons needed; OrbitControls replaced by custom orbit to keep a single CDN dependency).
- The app's own `fatal()` panel shows a user-friendly "HANGAR OFFLINE" message if CDNs are unreachable — worth mentioning in the final answer (network required; all else is inline).
- `dust` cloud positions are local to a group at (0,0,39) so rotating the Points doesn't drift it outside the door-light region.
- Formation label shows GRID (4×2) / SCATTER (per-drone golden-angle orbits); cinematic is a separate toggle — matches the requested "drone formation toggle and cinematic camera path".
- If the smoke test passes, no further code changes are planned; remaining work is purely reporting.
- No background jobs are running; nothing else is pending in the workspace.

Done — the smoke test passes end-to-end. Final state verified:

**Deliverable: [`hangar20.html`](hangar20.html)** — one self-contained 800-line / 37 KB HTML file in the workspace, all app code and styles inline.

**What's in the scene**
- **Hangar** — 56×16×120 m single-sided room (exterior views get a cutaway "dollhouse" look), trusses, ribs, windows, a glowing wall sign, a 36×13 m open door with 5 top slats spilling door light + mist shafts into the hangar.
- **Hovering drones** — 8 procedurally built quads (body, dome, fins, 4 spinning rotors, cyan/amber LEDs, thruster glow, per-drone soft shadow discs). **Formation toggle (F / button)**: GRID 4×2 ↔ SCATTER (per-drone golden-angle orbits), with damped lerp, shortest-arc yaw, and bank from lateral velocity.
- **Warning lights** — 3 rotating beacons (2 red, 1 amber, sweeping lights), 10-segment marching warning bar at the door, 4 strobes, flickering ceiling strips.
- **Runway** — emissive side strips, amber center dashes, and a landing pad with a 28-segment chase ring, decal ring/cross, and hazard chevrons at the door threshold.
- **Volumetric-style fog** — 11 slowly rotating additive fog planes + 3 mist shafts + 260 drifting dust motes in the door light (all procedural `CanvasTexture`, `fog:false` additive so glow survives `FogExp2`).
- **Cinematic camera (C / button)** — closed Catmull-Rom path (8 control points, 85 s loop) with a lookAt that eases between the pad and drone 0. Shares the same damped-pose pipeline as the custom orbit (drag/scroll, clamped), so switching modes handoffs seamlessly. **R / Reset** restores the default view.
- **Rendering** — physical lighting (candela point lights, hemi), `ACESFilmicToneMapping` @ 1.12 exposure, sRGB, no post-processing (glow is faked with additive sprites/planes). HUD shows formation/camera/UAV status; a "HANGAR OFFLINE" panel appears if the CDN is unreachable.

**Verification performed**
- JS syntax check on the extracted module: clean (`node --check`).
- Headless smoke test (Node + Proxy-stubbed WebGL/document, real three.js r160 module): scene constructs, **8 frames rendered** covering manual orbit, cinematic mode, all three key/button toggles, and resize — `SMOKE TEST PASSED`.
- All 3 CDN fallback URLs (jsdelivr → unpkg → cdnjs) return HTTP 200; all 31 `THREE.*` names used resolve against the r160 export surface.

**To run:** open the file directly in any modern browser (needs network access for the single external dependency, three.js 0.160.0 from CDN) or serve the directory (`python3 -m http.server`) and visit `http://localhost:8000/hangar20.html`.
